title.rendered: Power to Get Wealth: The Gospel For Today

content.rendered:
You shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, that He may establish His covenant which He swore to your fathers, as it is this day. The Father delegates. He delegates authority. He delegates spiritual power. He also delegates the ability to produce.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, August 8, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And you shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, that He may establish His covenant which He swore to your fathers, as it is this day.”
Deuteronomy 8:18 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Moses is delivering his final address to Israel on the plains of Moab, just before the nation crosses the Jordan into the promised land. He is preparing them for a season of unprecedented prosperity. The land is going to be good. The crops are going to come in. The herds are going to multiply. The houses are going to be full. And in the middle of that abundance, Moses warns them not to make one specific mistake. Do not, when you are prospering, forget who gave you the power to prosper.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition renders it: “But you shall [earnestly] remember the Lord your God, for it is He Who gives you power to get wealth, that He may establish His covenant which He swore to your fathers, as it is this day” (Deuteronomy 8:18 AMPC). Earnestly remember. The verb is intense. Not a passing thought. A committed act of memory that keeps the source of the wealth clear.

Two things are worth noting carefully. First, the Bible does not condemn wealth. The Bible names God as the giver of the power to produce it. Moses does not say, “God will bless you with wealth despite Himself.” Moses says God gives the power to get wealth. This is a delegated ability, like every other authority we have walked through in this series. The believer walking with God has been given the capacity to produce, to build, to steward, to accumulate resources that establish the covenant purposes of God in the earth.

Second, Moses names the purpose of the wealth. That He may establish His covenant. The prosperity is not for personal aggrandisement. It is for the establishment of God’s purposes in the earth. Wealth in the hands of the covenant-keeping believer is a tool. It funds gospel expansion. It feeds the hungry. It provides for widows and orphans. It builds Kingdom infrastructure. It relieves the persecuted. It sends missionaries. The believer whose power to produce is aligned with God’s covenant purpose becomes a channel of God’s own generosity to the earth.

The New Testament echoes this. Paul teaches in 2 Corinthians 9:8 that God is able to make all grace abound to the believer, so that always having all sufficiency in all things, they may have abundance for every good work. In 1 Timothy 6:17-19, Paul instructs the rich in this present age not to be conceited or to trust in uncertain riches, but to trust in the living God who gives us richly all things to enjoy, so that they may do good, be rich in good works, ready to give, willing to share. The power to produce and the purpose of the produce belong together in New Testament theology.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is honouring and challenging. Honouring because the Lord has given you real, delegated ability to produce, to work, to earn, to build. Challenging because that ability is not for yourself alone. It is for the establishment of the covenant of God in the earth. Remember Him today. Thank Him for the power to produce. And use what you produce to fund what He is doing.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have given me the power to get wealth. Every skill I have, every gift I carry, every opportunity that comes across my path, every relationship that opens a door, is from You. I remember You today as the source of the power to produce. I refuse to forget where the ability came from. I use what You have entrusted to me to establish Your covenant in the earth. My wealth funds the gospel. My provision feeds the hungry. My abundance provides for the persecuted. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The Lord gives me power to get wealth to establish His covenant. Every ability I have to produce is from Him. I remember Him and steward what He gives for His Kingdom.

Go Deeper in the Word

  • 2 Corinthians 9:8-11 (NKJV): God makes all grace abound for every good work
  • 1 Timothy 6:17-19 (NKJV): Instructions to the rich in this present age
